title: 資材値上がり、不漁、燃料高騰…ホタテ漁「まさに三重苦」　原油不安、農林水産業を直撃
extracted_text: 米イスラエルのイラン攻撃によって、エネルギー供給の要衝ホルムズ海峡を巡る情勢が混乱したことを受けた原油の供給不安が、日本各地の農林水産業にも深刻な影響を及ぼしている。ボイラー、包装材、燃料…。生産コストの値上がりは避けがたく、食卓へのしわ寄せも懸念される。 「赤字を覚悟しなければならないかもしれないが」。山形市のサクランボ農家、鈴木淳さん（50）はこう嘆く。 寒い時期はビニールハウスで成長を促すため、重油で暖房用のボイラーを動かして室温を上げるが、需要が見込める10日の「母の日」商戦を前に夜間の温度を7度から5度まで下げざるを得なかった。 全国納豆鑑評会で2度の最優秀賞受賞歴のある「川中島納豆」を製造する長野市の増屋納豆店は、容器の仕入れ先から1日から発泡ポリスチレン容器を約20％、ポリエチレン製の被膜を約35％値上げするという連絡を受けた。 容器は納豆の出来具合にも影響し、安易に変更できない。西條（さいじょう）純一社長（59）は「包装や配送用段ボール箱なども値上がりしているので、納豆の値上げも検討せざるを得ない」と話した。
translated_text: The turmoil surrounding the Strait of Hormuz — a critical corridor for global energy supplies — triggered by the Israel-Hamas conflict has sent shockwaves through Japan’s agricultural, forestry, and fisheries sectors. Rising production costs for boilers, packaging materials, and fuel have become unavoidable, raising concerns about the knock-on effect on food prices at the dinner table. “We may have to accept losses.” That is the lament of Jun Suzuki, a 50-year-old cherry farmer in Yamagata city. During the cold months, he uses diesel to fire greenhouse boilers to keep temperatures up for growth. But with Mother’s Day — May 10 — expected to bring strong demand, he has been forced to lower nighttime temperatures from 7 degrees to 5 degrees to save on fuel costs. Meanwhile, Masuya Natto Shop in Nagano city — maker of the award-winning Kawanakajima Natto, which has won top honors twice at the National Natto Competition — received notice from its container supplier on May 1 that expanded polystyrene containers would rise by approximately 20 percent and polyethylene film by roughly 35 percent. Containers affect the quality of the natto, so the change cannot be made lightly. Junichi Saijo, the 59-year-old president of the company, said, “Packaging and cardboard boxes for shipping have also gone up in price, so we will have no choice but to consider raising the price of natto.”
title_en: Rising Materials, Fuel Costs Hit Scallop Fishery with Triple Blow — Oil Crisis Squeezes Agriculture, Fisheries Across Japan
